newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee market attracts demand for early '97.
newsitem.headline: German coffee market attracts demand for early '97.

text.p: German coffee roasters are seeking to buy green beans for early 1997 as nearby supplies are unavailable and futures are firmer, traders said on Monday.
"Consumers a fortnight ago were hoping for New York (arabicas) to move below 100 cents/lb (December)," one said.
"Now they don't rule out 120 cents and that has resulted in some interest because new season shipments seem to be getting off to a slow start."
Outright sales volumes were still comparatively moderate because roasters were adequately covered, he added.
But some traders were reportedly short of near-term Central Americans and southern European consumers were less well supplied than the Germans.
The New York December position closed on Friday near an earlier six-week high at 116.30 cents.
London robustas took their lead from New York this morning although the increases were below expectations.
Physical robustas were being ordered for the first quarter of 1997 as differentials eased on expectations of a large Vietnamese 1996/97 crop.
Traders reported sales of Indonesian, Vietnamese, Ugandan and Ivorian robustas.
In the Bremen import market, Brazils were offered at $115 per 50 kg fob, up $7 on the week, and Colombia Excelso was at $134, up $8.
Kenyan prices rose sharply to $156 from $139 a week earlier and Indonesian robustas stayed at $65.
